## Overview

**Core question:** Does a transfer-capable optimal-tiled color image preserve its exact buffer representation through a buffer-to-image copy followed by an image-to-buffer copy on the universal queue?

- [`vktImageTransfer.cpp`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L57-L292) implements `image.queue_transfer`. Each leaf allocates host-visible source and destination buffers, uploads generated bytes to the source buffer, copies them through one image, and compares every returned byte with the original.
- The test uses one primary command buffer and the universal queue; despite the group's name, it does not transfer queue-family ownership between queues.
- There is no shader program in this family: [`TransferQueueCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L72-L75) is empty. The observable result comes entirely from transfer commands, barriers, and host readback.

## Background Knowledge

For the shared concepts subresources, copies, layouts, and synchronization, see [Background Knowledge](../../categories/image.md#background-knowledge) of the `image` page.

- **Buffer-image copies.** `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage` and `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` move texel data between a buffer and an image subresource. A `VkBufferImageCopy` identifies the buffer layout, image subresource layers, offset, and extent used by both commands.
- **Image layouts and transfer ordering.** An image begins in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED`. Before the first copy, this test transitions it to `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL`; a second barrier makes transfer writes available to the following transfer read while preserving that layout.
- **Host-visible memory synchronization.** The host flushes the source allocation before submission and invalidates the destination allocation after the queue completes. These operations make the host writes available to the device and the device writes available to the host before byte comparison.

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
image.queue_transfer
├── 2d
├── 2d_array
└── 3d
```

[`createTransferQueueImageTests()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L309-L368) creates the three direct image-class groups, and [`createChildren()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTests.cpp#L61-L100) registers `queue_transfer` under `image`. The hierarchy is present in the default mustpass inventory in [`queue-transfer.txt`](../../../mustpass/main/vk-default/image/queue-transfer.txt).

## Parameter Dimensions and Observed Values

| Dimension | Registered values | Meaning in this test | Evidence |
|-----------|-------------------|----------------------|----------|
| Image class | `2d`, `2d_array`, `3d` | Selects `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D` with one layer, `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D` with several layers, or `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_3D` with depth. | [Class array](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L313-L325) |
| Extent leaf | `4x3x1`, `16x15x1`, `64x31x1`, `4x3x2`, `16x15x16` | Supplies width, height, and the source depth value. | [Extent array](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L327-L336) |
| Color format | Every entry in `formats::basicColorFormats` | Selects the image format, format-mapped byte representation, generated input data, and leaf suffix. | [Format loop](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L348-L359) |
| 2D layer count | `1` for `2d`; extent depth for `2d_array` | For 2D images, the source depth field becomes the number of array layers. | [Layer/depth selection](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L168-L172) |
| 3D depth | Extent depth for `3d` | For 3D images, the source depth field becomes the image extent depth; array layer count remains one. | [Layer/depth selection](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L168-L172) |
| Image configuration | One mip level, sample count 1, optimal tiling, transfer source and destination usage | Fixes the resource model while the groups vary shape and format. | [Image create info](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L188-L206) |

The primary behavioral axis is **image class**. It selects whether the copy region addresses one 2D layer, several 2D array layers, or a 3D volume. Extent and basic-color-format dimensions provide coverage for that same transfer sequence. The current default mustpass inventories contain 131 formats per image-class/extent combination for Vulkan and 129 for Vulkan SC; unsupported formats are absent from the corresponding inventory.

## Behavior Parameters

### `2d` - One-layer 2D image

`2d` creates a `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D` image with one array layer. The extent-depth field remains one for the registered 2D cases, so both copy commands cover one color subresource layer.

### `2d_array` - Layered 2D image

`2d_array` also uses `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D`, but the selected extent-depth field becomes the image's array-layer count. The transfer region sets `layerCount` to that count, which checks packed buffer data across every selected layer.

### `3d` - Three-dimensional image

`3d` uses `VK_IMAGE_TYPE_3D` with one array layer. The selected extent-depth field instead becomes the image depth and the Z extent of the copy region. This path checks volume transfer addressing rather than array-layer addressing.

## Shader Analysis

This family has no shader program. [`TransferQueueCase::initPrograms()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L72-L75) is empty; the two Vulkan transfer commands, their image barriers, and host-side byte comparison define the tested behavior.

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

For every leaf, [`TransferQueueInstance::iterate()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L157-L292) performs the following sequence.

1. It maps the selected `VkFormat` to a TCU format and computes the source and destination buffer size as pixel size times width, height, layers, and depth. It creates both buffers with transfer-source and transfer-destination usage in host-visible memory.
2. It creates a one-mip image with `VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL`, `VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT`, exclusive sharing, and an initial `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED` layout.
3. It generates format-appropriate non-NaN bytes with a seed derived from the selected format, image type, and extent, copies those bytes into the source allocation, and flushes that allocation. [Data generation and upload](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L208-L219).
4. The command buffer transitions the color subresource from undefined to general layout. It then records `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage`. The copy region covers mip level zero and all layers; it uses zero `bufferRowLength`, a block-height-rounded `bufferImageHeight`, and the selected image extent. [Transition and copy-region setup](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L221-L266).
5. A transfer-stage image barrier changes access from transfer write to transfer read without changing `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL`. The command buffer then records `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` using the same region. [Post-copy barrier and copyback](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L248-L273).
6. After `submitCommandsAndWait()` completes, the host invalidates the destination allocation, copies its bytes to a vector, and compares it against the generated bytes. The case fails on the first unequal byte; otherwise it returns `Pass`. [Submission and byte oracle](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L275-L292).

### Transfer Command Flow

```text
host-generated bytes
    │ flush
    ▼
source buffer
    │ vkCmdCopyBufferToImage
    ▼
image: UNDEFINED → GENERAL
    │ transfer-write → transfer-read barrier
    ▼
image: GENERAL
    │ vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer
    ▼
destination buffer
    │ queue completion + invalidate
    ▼
byte-for-byte comparison with generated bytes
```

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `2d` | One-layer 2D buffer-image copy handling, selected-format transfer representation, layout transition, transfer ordering, or host readback. |
| `2d_array` | Array-layer count or layer addressing in the copy region, image creation, buffer packing, or a failure shared with the ordinary round-trip path. |
| `3d` | Three-dimensional extent or depth handling in either copy direction, the intervening transfer dependency, or a failure shared with the ordinary round-trip path. |

A failure that spans several image classes can also indicate shared command submission, destination-allocation invalidation, or round-trip copy handling.

### Cause Analysis

#### Copy-region or dimensional interpretation

**Possible failure symptoms:** A mismatch is limited to array or 3D leaves, or appears only when the depth value is greater than one.

**Possible implementation causes:** The source gives 2D arrays a layer count equal to the selected extent depth, but gives 3D images one array layer and an image extent depth equal to that value. The same `VkBufferImageCopy` region is used for upload and copyback, so incorrect layer/depth interpretation in either direction changes the compared byte sequence. [Parameter mapping](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L168-L172) and [copy region](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L234-L246) define those paths.

#### Layout, visibility, or host readback

**Possible failure symptoms:** Many unrelated formats or dimensions return corrupted or stale destination bytes.

**Possible implementation causes:** The image must reach general layout before the buffer-to-image copy, and its transfer writes must be made available for the later image-to-buffer read. After completion, the destination allocation must be invalidated before host access. A defect in those transitions, dependencies, submission, or host-memory visibility can affect otherwise unrelated leaves. [Barriers](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L221-L227) [post-copy dependency](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L248-L271) [readback](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L277-L289).

#### Format-specific transfer representation

**Possible failure symptoms:** Failures cluster under one format suffix, particularly where block handling differs from ordinary texels.

**Possible implementation causes:** The transfer region uses a block-height-rounded `bufferImageHeight` when the selected format is compressed, while generated data, buffer size, and comparison derive from the selected TCU format and dimensions. Incorrect implementation handling of the selected format's transfer representation can therefore produce a byte mismatch. The source's failure status does not further distinguish the command or stage that introduced a particular differing byte. [Compressed-format branch](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L230-L245) [byte comparison](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L283-L289).

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

- [`TransferQueueCase::checkSupport()`](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L109-L140) queries image-format properties for the selected format, image type, optimal tiling, and the combined transfer-source and transfer-destination usage. `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` skips the leaf; another error fails it.
- The same callback reads optimal-tiling format features. Its literal check skips a format only when **neither** `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT` nor `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT` is set; the preceding image-format-properties query tests the actual combined image usage requested by the case.
- Outside Vulkan SC, `VK_FORMAT_A8_UNORM_KHR` and `VK_FORMAT_A1B5G5R5_UNORM_PACK16_KHR` require `VK_KHR_maintenance5`. [Conditional requirement](../../../modules/vulkan/image/vktImageTransfer.cpp#L114-L117).

### Design-based pruning

- Registration includes only `formats::basicColorFormats`; depth/stencil, multiplane, and other format lists are not added by this factory.
- The factory fixes one mip level, one sample, color aspect, optimal tiling, exclusive sharing, and a single universal queue. It varies image class, extent, and color format rather than queue-family ownership, sampling, or subresource selection.

## Key Takeaways

- `image.queue_transfer` is a transfer-command round-trip test, not a queue-family ownership-transfer test and not a shader test.
- Every leaf uses the same `buffer → image → buffer` sequence and exact byte comparison; image class, extent, and basic color format define the coverage matrix.
- The test explicitly exercises an undefined-to-general layout transition, transfer-write-to-transfer-read ordering, and host-memory flush/invalidate around the two copy commands.
- A passing leaf demonstrates that the returned destination bytes exactly match the generated source bytes for that registered image configuration.
